brique._comment: Engine-native Reflexive family capacity. kind/wrapper/rel_ctx/lang do not apply here.

objective.name: edit.create
objective.description: Create one or more local Brique elements in the current context tree.

#root.role: Validate one creation batch, materialize the requested local elements or contexts, and return one aggregated per-item result payload.

items._comment: Required non-empty creation batch. Each item: { type (string: context|capacity|schema|document), name (string), content_json (optional string — JSON object seed for the descriptor), destination_ctx_id (optional string — absolute context path, defaults to addressed context) }.

result._comment: Per-item result list. Each item: { ok (bool), type (string), name (string) } on success, or { ok: false, type, name, error: { code, message, reason } } on per-item failure.

effects.context_tree: Local directories, files, and meaning descriptors may be created under the current context.

transformation_contract.morphing: A batch of local element creation requests becomes a per-item creation result set, with successful items materializing new local Brique elements in the current context tree.
invariants: edit.create is batch-oriented and returns one result entry per parsed item.
Context creation materializes the child context directory tree plus required subdirectories and updates the parent child list.
Non-context creation writes a meaning descriptor from either provided content or the embedded template for the requested type.
Embedded template order is preserved, and content_json is authoritative when supplied so caller-defined key order is preserved.
success: On success, each result item reports ok=true with the normalized type and name of the created element.
Document creation can also create an empty local content file when the created document resolves to a local file target.
failure: The capacity fails when params.items is missing or cannot be parsed into a valid edit batch.
Individual items return errors when the target type is unsupported, the name is invalid or already exists, the target escapes scope, or the descriptor/template cannot be written.
notes: Matter and structure creates are refused here because those element kinds are owned by MatterLoop.
Structured content objects remain supported for compatibility but cannot preserve caller key order after map decoding; use content_json when descriptor order matters.
Templates are loaded from the embedded engine template set when item content is not supplied.
